item.mechanism: Nanocrystalline grain size combined with grain boundary strengthening hinders dislocation movement, leading to high hardness.
item.system: Equimolar CuMoTaWV RHEA film (nanocrystalline, ~18 nm grain size)
item.operating_conditions: As-deposited state, room temperature, nanoindentation at 3 mN load
item.supporting_observation: Average hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and Young's modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa were measured.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism is specific to the nanocrystalline regime; grain growth at higher annealing temperatures (400–500 °C) reduces nanocrystallinity and increases roughness, potentially altering the mechanism.
item.alternatives_considered: Solid solution hardening alone is insufficient; the text emphasizes the combined effect of nanocrystallinity and grain boundaries.
quotes: High hardness in a metallic film can be related to the enhanced grain boundary strengthening from nanocrystallinity.
The dislocation movement is hindered within the columnar grains during plastic deformation.
The nanocrystalline nature of the RHEA film resulted in a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.

item.mechanism: Solid solution hardening combined with grain boundary strengthening results in extremely high compressive strength in nanopillars.
item.operating_conditions: Microcompression at room temperature, load control mode up to 3 mN
item.supporting_observation: Average yield strength of 10.7 ± 0.8 GPa was observed, attributed to combined solid solution and grain boundary effects.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism shifts from dislocation-controlled to grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation in small pillars, leading to intergranular fracture.
item.alternatives_considered: Dislocation-controlled plastic deformation is dominant in larger pillars but shifts in nanoscale pillars.
quotes: The extremely high compressional strength of the BCC HEA nanopillar has been attributed to the combined effect of a substantial solid solution hardening effect, grain size, and grain boundary strengthening.
Thus, the strengthening mechanism in nanopillar HEAs shifts from dislocation-controlled to grain-boundary-controlled plastic deformation, which eventually leads to intergranular fracture.
A high compressive strength of 10 ± 0.8 GPa was obtained in nanopillar compression due to solid solution hardening and grain boundary strengthening.

item.mechanism: Annealing at 300 °C improves film adhesion and reduces surface roughness, preventing film removal and stabilizing friction.
item.system: CuMoTaWV RHEA film on 304 stainless-steel substrate
item.operating_conditions: Annealing at 300 °C in argon atmosphere; wear testing at RT and 300 °C
item.supporting_observation: Annealed film showed steady-state COF of 0.25 and low wear rates, whereas as-deposited film showed film removal and COF increase to 0.7.
item.scope_limits: Annealing above 300 °C (e.g., 400 °C) decreases nanocrystallinity and increases surface roughness, potentially negating benefits.
item.alternatives_considered: As-deposited films suffer from low adhesion leading to excessive plastic deformation and smearing.
quotes: The adhesion between the RHEA film and 304 stainless-steel substrates was increased on annealing.
Annealing the CuMoTaWV RHEA film at 300 °C improved the surface roughness through grain refinement and increased the adhesion of the film to the steel substrate.

The wear behavior of the annealed high-entropy film showed an average COF of 0.25 up to a 30 m sliding distance, followed by a slight increase to 0.3, and remained the same until the end of the test, suggesting an improvement in the film response to wear and its adhesion to the substrate on annealing.

item.mechanism: Formation of CuO during high-temperature sliding reduces wear rate by forming a protective tribofilm.
item.system: CuMoTaWV RHEA film on 304 stainless-steel substrate
item.operating_conditions: Wear test at 300 °C against E52100 alloy steel counterball
item.supporting_observation: Wear track analysis showed high Cu content, linked to CuO formation, correlating with stable wear behavior despite high COF.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism is specific to moderate temperatures (300 °C) where tribochemical reactions occur; at RT, wear is lower and COF is lower without this oxide formation.
item.alternatives_considered: High COF at 300 °C is attributed to tribochemical reaction with the steel counterball, but the wear rate remains low due to CuO.
quotes: The wear track from the high-temperature wear test at 300 °C showed a high amount of Cu in the wear, which can be related to the formation of CuO.
The frictional and wear behavior of the annealed high-entropy film can be related to its high hardness, nanocrystallinity, and better adhesion.

item.mechanism: Lattice distortion and sluggish diffusion hinder island growth during sputtering, resulting in nanocrystalline grain formation.
item.system: CuMoTaWV RHEA film deposited via DC-magnetron sputtering
item.operating_conditions: Deposition at 500 °C substrate temperature in argon atmosphere
item.supporting_observation: Grain size calculated as 18 nm, significantly smaller than cosputtered films, attributed to high distortion and sluggish diffusion.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism relies on the presence of high lattice distortion; cosputtering from multiple targets may result in weaker sluggish diffusion and larger grains.
item.alternatives_considered: Island growth is the typical mechanism, but it is hindered here by the unique HEA characteristics.
quotes: However, due to the presence of a high amount of distortion, the island growth is hindered by sluggish diffusion, one of the prime characteristics of high-entropy alloys, and leads to the formation of nanocrystalline grains.
The reduced lattice constant can be related to the presence of Cu atoms having a smaller atomic radius than those of the other refractory atoms, which will reduce the lattice parameter.
The nanocrystalline nature of the RHEA film resulted in a hardness of 19 ± 2.3 GPa and an elastic modulus of 259 ± 19.2 GPa.

item.mechanism: High sputtering rate of refractory elements relative to Cu leads to surface enrichment of refractory elements and depletion of Cu.
item.operating_conditions: As-deposited state, analyzed via XPS and EDS
item.supporting_observation: Surface Cu content was ~3 atom % (EDS) and ~0.7–0.8 atom % (XPS), significantly lower than the equimolar target composition.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism explains surface composition deviation but does not account for bulk composition which remains closer to equimolar.
item.alternatives_considered: Segregation of elements was ruled out by uniform elemental mapping, suggesting sputtering yield differences.
quotes: The low amount of Cu can be related to the high sputtering of refractory elements, which could have resulted in more scattering of Cu atoms in the sputtering plasma after initial deposition.
The EDS area analysis of the film surface showed an equiatomic composition, except for Cu, which was found in a low amount of ∼3 atom %.
The XPS analysis showed a uniform distribution of elements with a low amount of Cu.

item.mechanism: Lattice mismatch between film and substrate induces stress, leading to an initial dense amorphous-like interfacial layer.
item.system: CuMoTaWV RHEA film on Si substrate
item.operating_conditions: As-deposited state, analyzed via cross-section SEM
item.supporting_observation: Initial ~10 nm dense film observed at interface, attributed to ~41% lattice mismatch causing tremendous stress.
item.scope_limits: Specific to the Si substrate interface; the bulk of the film forms a BCC solid solution.
item.alternatives_considered: No other interfacial mechanisms were proposed; the stress is directly linked to the lattice parameter difference.
quotes: The initial film deposition at the film–Si substrate interface showed the formation of a dense film of ∼10 nm.

The initial dense deposition can be related to the formation of an amorphous film due to a lattice mismatch of ∼41% between the CuMoTaWV RHEA film (3.18 Å) and the Si crystal (5.43 Å), resulting in tremendous stress in the film.
The experimentally determined lattice parameter is 3.18 Å, which is in good agreement with the one for the DFT-optimized SQS (3.16 Å).

item.mechanism: Partial sintering of elemental powders via Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) creates a single consolidated target that ensures uniform evaporation of all elements.
item.operating_conditions: SPS at 1000 °C, 40 MPa pressure, vacuum atmosphere
item.supporting_observation: Elemental maps showed uniform distribution of all phases in the target cross-section, ensuring plasma evaporation of all principal elements.
item.scope_limits: Mechanism applies to the target preparation process; the resulting film properties depend on subsequent sputtering parameters.
item.alternatives_considered: Cosputtering from multiple targets was considered but resulted in nonhomogeneous distribution and weaker sluggish diffusion.
quotes: The elemental maps from the cross section of the target in Figure 1 b showed a uniform distribution of all of the elemental phases.
This suggests that in the DC sputter film from the single target, the plasma will evaporate all of the principal elements to the substrate.
A single target containing the principal elements, CuMoTaWV, was partially sintered at 1000 °C using SPS to lower the cost and time of target preparation.
